# Intel and Oracle Plan Expanded Collaboration to Support Enterprise and Agentic AI on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

- Print

- Email

- Copy Link

ORACLE AI WORLD, LAS VEGAS – October 27, 2026 — Intel and Oracle today announced plans for a multiyear collaboration intended to expand Intel® Xeon®-based computing on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The collaboration is intended to meet the growing demand for enterprise applications, agentic AI, and inference, and is expected to span current and future Xeon platforms, including planned OCI X14 offerings based on Intel’s next-generation server processor codenamed Diamond Rapids .

As more enterprises deploy AI agents at scale, CPUs are becoming increasingly critical for executing applications, managing data movement, orchestrating agentic actions and supporting inference across existing business systems. The expanded collaboration between Intel and Oracle is intended to support additional capacity and planned processor capabilities as customers extend existing enterprise systems with AI, while retaining familiar software environments and operational tooling.

"As AI agents scale, they need processors that can run software, move and secure data, and accelerate inference. Xeon brings together performance and hardware-based confidential computing, giving organizations a trusted, cost-effective foundation for AI at scale," said Kevork Kechichian, executive vice president and general manager, Intel Data Center Group. "Our expanded collaboration with Oracle is intended to combine Intel's multigenerational roadmap with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's technology to help customers put AI to work faster and more cost-effectively."

Building on their decades-long relationship, Intel and Oracle intend to coordinate roadmaps and processor capacity planning to support OCI’s expansion. Planned Diamond Rapids-based OCI X14 offerings are expected to bring advances in both AI acceleration and general-purpose computing, including enhanced Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) with FP8, FP16, and BF16 support for optimized inference software, and Intel Advanced Performance Extensions (APX) to help optimized applications execute with less instruction overhead. Together, these innovations are expected to help organizations integrate AI into existing enterprise environments, with capabilities that support embedding generation, reranking, and smaller-model inference alongside the application services and tools AI agents use.

“Enterprise AI depends on the applications, data, and tools that let an agent complete useful work,” said Pradeep Vincent, executive vice president, compute and AI infrastructure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle. “Our expanded collaboration with Intel is intended to help us grow the compute capacity behind those workloads and support plans to bring enhanced Xeon capabilities to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure through X14. Customers are expected to gain a path to build and scale AI using the enterprise software environments they already rely on.”

OCI’s current Xeon-based offerings pair Intel compute with built-in AI acceleration, flexible CPU and memory configurations, and Oracle Acceleron networking. Organizations can tailor application services, data processing, and agent execution to their needs while scaling each independently of the accelerators serving larger models. As a result, customers can better match resources to each stage of an AI workflow and manage overall application costs.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Intel GPU D270?

Intel GPU D270 is an inference-optimized data center GPU designed for the agentic AI era. It is built to support enterprise AI, SaaS, GPUaaS, and government or sovereign-cloud deployments that need memory-rich, power-efficient AI acceleration.

### What types of AI workloads is Intel GPU D270 designed to support?

Intel GPU D270 is designed for production AI inference workloads such as agentic AI, long-context retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), enterprise AI assistants, coding assistants, document understanding, multimodal AI, diffusion models, and high-concurrency serving.

### Why is Intel GPU D270 relevant for agentic AI?

Agentic AI often turns one task into multiple rounds of model calls, tool use, retrieval, reasoning, and response generation. Intel GPU D270 is designed for the inference requirements that become important in those environments, including prefill processing, larger context, memory capacity, concurrency, and power efficiency.

### What does “inference-optimized” mean for Intel GPU D270?

Inference-optimized means the GPU is designed for running AI models in production rather than training them at massive scale. Intel GPU D270 focuses on the needs of deployed AI applications, including prompt processing, high-concurrency serving, memory capacity, efficient power use, and system-level performance.

### How does Intel GPU D270 help with long-context AI workloads?

Long-context AI workloads can require more memory to support larger prompts, retrieval-heavy workflows, and KV cache growth during inference. Intel GPU D270 is designed with high available memory capacity to help support larger models, longer context, and more concurrent sessions.

### What software frameworks are relevant to Intel GPU D270?

Intel GPU D270 messaging should reference familiar AI software and serving frameworks such as PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, and OpenAI Triton, where approved. This helps developers and platform teams understand how the product fits into existing AI workflows.

### Can Intel GPU D270 be used in existing data center infrastructure?

Intel GPU D270 is designed around a standard PCIe 5.0 form factor and air-cooled deployment profile, helping enterprises evaluate AI inference acceleration within existing data center environments without requiring a specialized liquid-cooling retrofit.

### Who is the primary audience for Intel GPU D270?

The primary audience includes AI system architects, AI platform architects, infrastructure and cloud engineering leaders, enterprise AI decision-makers, SaaS providers, GPUaaS providers, government or sovereign-cloud teams, and developers deploying production inference workloads.

### What should customers do if they want to learn more about Intel GPU D270?

Customers should connect with Intel to learn more about Intel GPU D270, evaluate how it may fit their AI inference roadmap, and receive updates as additional product information becomes available.
